sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the difference between love and fear is that love comes from a revelation of light from above, while fear comes primarily from man's service, and therefore in Elul, which is the service of "I am for my Beloved," there must be fear, specifically the acceptance of the yoke of the kingdom of heaven, which is aroused by the shofar.

translations.translation: And one can explain the elucidation of this,
that from the distinctions between love and fear is,
that love comes through a revelation of light from above,
and fear comes
(primarily)
through the service of man.
And analogous to fear of a mortal king,
that the reason the people of the land fear the king is because they have accepted him to be king over them,
for the acceptance of the kingship is by the people,
"You shall surely set a king over you."
Therefore,
since in Elul it is the service of "I am for my Beloved,"
the service of man,
there must then be fear.
And one should add,
that the primary service in Elul,
"I am for my Beloved,"
is the acceptance of the yoke of the kingdom of heaven.
For this is what is said in Likkutei Torah, that the service of Elul is the going out to the field to greet the face of the king.
And that which they blow the shofar
(in Elul)
to arouse fear and trembling,
it is,
because the concept of "You shall surely set a king over you" is that his awe be upon you,
and in order that the acceptance of the kingship be complete, it is specifically through the arousal of fear.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section elaborates that the shofar blasts in Elul arouse lower-level fear as a preparation for the higher-level fear aroused by the shofar on Rosh Hashanah, and that the drawing down of the encompassing light on Rosh Hashanah requires the self-nullification and trembling that come from the shofar of Elul.

translations.translation: And the explanation of the concept in more detail will be understood according to what the Tzemach Tzedek said in a discourse,
that explains the concept of the shofar blast on Rosh Chodesh Elul,
that this blowing of the shofar in the month of Elul is a preparation for the shofar blast of Rosh Hashanah.
For the distinction between the shofar blast of Elul and the shofar blast of Rosh Hashanah is,
that the fear
(and trembling)
that comes through the shofar blast of Elul is lower-level fear,
and the fear
(and trembling)
that comes through the shofar blast of Rosh Hashanah is higher-level fear.
And this is why they instituted blowing the shofar on Rosh Chodesh Elul and throughout the month,
because in order to come to higher-level fear, one must first have lower-level fear.
And another reason for this, that they blow the shofar in the month of Elul before Rosh Hashanah, is,
because during the Ten Days of Repentance,
beginning from Rosh Hashanah,
one must draw down from the encompassing light in order to fill that which they blemished during the entire year,
and the drawing down of the encompassing light is specifically through self-nullification.
And as explained in Torah Or
on the verse,
"The heavens are My throne and the earth is My footstool; which house... But to this one I will look: to the poor and broken of spirit,"
that "heavens" and "earth" are Torah and mitzvos,
for the drawing down through Torah and mitzvos is internal light,
"My throne" and "My footstool,"
and in order to draw down the encompassing lights,
"which house...,"
for "house" is an encompassing light
(and within the encompassing lights themselves, the distant encompassing light),
it is through self-nullification,
"the poor and broken of spirit and who trembles at My word."
And therefore they blow the shofar in Elul,
because in order for there to be the drawing down of the encompassing light on Rosh Hashanah, there must be "broken of spirit" and trembling,
and through the shofar blast they come to trembling.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section questions why the fear from the shofar of Elul is necessary for drawing down the encompassing light on Rosh Hashanah, since the fear on Rosh Hashanah itself is greater, and answers that it is specifically the fear from Elul that enables this drawing down.

translations.translation: And one must understand,
behold, also through blowing the shofar on Rosh Hashanah they come to trembling,
and on the contrary,
the trembling of Rosh Hashanah is greater than the trembling of Elul,
and as mentioned above in the discourse, that the trembling that comes from the shofar blast of Elul is lower-level fear,
and the trembling that comes from the shofar blast of Rosh Hashanah is higher-level fear.
And nevertheless,
the drawing down of the encompassing light on Rosh Hashanah is through the trembling that comes from the shofar blast of Elul.
